correctness.rationale: The ratios produce relaxed coordinate minimization of log Z. Positivity gives an affinely spanning support, positive definite covariance Hessian and compact sublevels (cosh lower bound). At fixed other coordinate the partition function is a positive factor times cosh((coordinate−minimizer)/2). Its argument is multiplied by h=1−ω at each half-step, yielding strict descent for |h|<1 except at the coordinate minimum, exact conservation for h=−1, and ascent for |h|>1 off that minimum. A sweep with zero decrement in the open interval is the unique balanced critical point; compactness and continuity give convergence. Conversely, convergence of either coupling would force ratio convergence (recover each ratio from two positive entries after dividing out K), so the higher-energy starts at and above 2 cannot converge to the balanced plan. At 0 the sweep is the identity. Averaging the log scales gives z'=h²z−ωh c(y)−ω d(x'); at equilibrium c=d=log Z and 1−h²=ω(1+h), yielding z→−log Z in the open interval. The log-ratio Jacobian has trace 2h+ω²ρ² and determinant h², with |ρ|<1 including ρ=0 for rank one; all three Schur inequalities are strict. It contracts locally in an adapted norm, and the driven scalar recurrence is geometrically convergent (enlarge the base slightly in case of coincident decay rates). Thus both normalized and actual coupling rates follow for the stated exact-data regime. Source diagnostics were read, not executed; no numerical premise is required.
